title: A more distant star's parallax
hook: Change distance and predict small annual parallax angle.
misconception: small annual parallax angle doubles when distance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply angle ≈ baseline/distance to compare small annual parallax angle when distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed observing baseline with distance much larger than that baseline, angle ≈ baseline/distance. When distance doubles, small annual parallax angle becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model angle ≈ baseline/distance; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed observing baseline with distance much larger than that baseline, with a nonzero initial result. If distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on small annual parallax angle?
recall.why: Apply angle ≈ baseline/distance under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
